pattern_stance_changes.reason: Table 1 directly measures fine-tuning against the un-tuned model on the same scaffold. Full SFT of Qwen3-8B on SWE-smith expert trajectories resolves 86 vs 19 SWE-bench Verified issues; on RepoQA Pass@0.8 the LoRA SFT scores 0.85 vs 0.65. This is a side baseline and the SFT run's variance is not reported (App. B covers only Base vs ICAE), but a +67-issue gap from a measured comparison clears the 'supports' bar.

missed_issues: The 'ICAE beats Base on single-shot' result is confounded by task fine-tuning. The ICAE encoder is fine-tuned on the SQuAD/RepoQA training data (§3) while Base is not, so the gain reflects tuning, not compression. Against SFT, the fair no-compression comparison, compression always costs accuracy (RepoQA Pass@0.8 0.69 vs 0.85; SQuAD EM 0.67 vs 0.70).
Floor effect: with thinking disabled and a 32k context, Base resolves only 19/500 (3.8%). The 12-issue gap may not transfer to frontier hosted models.

The '40% longer trajectories' are measured to a 32k context limit with no step limit (App. C). With a lower resolve rate, extra steps may be looping, as in the repeated README views in App. D, rather than useful work, so presenting them as an efficiency gain is questionable.
cherry_picked_examples: the App. D success demo is 'hand-crafted' and its environment was 'manually simulated by one of the authors'.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and the P08 'contradicts' stance, which applies only to learned latent compression, not host-side summarization. The single-shot 'gains' come from fine-tuning, not compression. The un-tuned vs SFT gap is genuine measured evidence for fine-tuning (P25).
